newsitem.title: ESTONIA: EBRD takes stake in Estonian Maapank.
newsitem.headline: EBRD takes stake in Estonian Maapank.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) on Wednesday signed a deal to make a three million mark investment, or a 19.4 percent stake, in Estonia's seventh largest bank, Maapank.
The bank also gained a 16 million Estonian kroon subordinated loan from Swedfund with a seven-year term.
"The EBRD sees itself as a medium to long term investor and we are not speculative investors," Jonathan Harfield, EBRD representive in Estonia, told a news conference.
"The three million mark equity investment will allow the bank to expand its banking activities and increase lending to private sector enterprises in Estonia," an EBRD statement added.
"The object of the loan is to provide risk capital and we do this before commercial investors come into the market," Tord Olofsson, Swedund president, told a news conference.
Olfsson was upbeat about Maapank, seeing it as a bank that has passed the grade in the local banking system.
Estonian banks are seen as the most advanced of the Baltic region after passing through a crisis in 1992. The EBRD has also taken stakes in Latvian and Lithuanian banks.
